title: Arabic for Non-Arabic Speakers – Level 01
overview: This beginner-level Arabic language course introduces non-Arabic-speaking learners to the essential sounds, script, vocabulary and sentence patterns needed for simple everyday communication. Through guided listening, speaking, reading and writing practice, participants learn to exchange basic personal information, understand familiar expressions and navigate common social situations. The course emphasizes practical Modern Standard Arabic while introducing useful everyday expressions, with supportive pronunciation practice and cultural context. No previous knowledge of Arabic is required.
audience: Non-Arabic-speaking adults beginning their study of Arabic.
Expatriate professionals and residents seeking basic communication skills in Arabic-speaking environments.
Customer-facing employees who interact with Arabic-speaking colleagues or visitors.
Learners preparing to progress to Arabic Level 02.
methodology: Trainer-led demonstrations and guided pronunciation drills; visual vocabulary activities; short listening dialogues; paired speaking tasks and role-plays; script tracing and writing practice; reading exercises; cultural scenarios; frequent formative checks; and an integrated end-of-course communication assessment. Activities are differentiated for learners unfamiliar with the Arabic alphabet.
competencies: Recognizing and producing common Arabic sounds and letter forms.
Reading and writing familiar words and short basic sentences.
Using essential greetings, introductions and polite expressions.
Understanding simple questions and short everyday exchanges.
Communicating basic personal, numerical, time and location information.
Applying foundational Arabic grammar in familiar contexts.
Demonstrating awareness of appropriate language use and cultural etiquette.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Identify Arabic letters in their principal written forms and pronounce common letter–sound combinations.
Read and write familiar words and short phrases with increasing accuracy.
Greet others, introduce themselves and exchange simple personal information.
Ask and answer basic questions about people, places, objects and daily routines.
Use numbers, dates, times and everyday vocabulary in simple interactions.
Construct short affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences using beginner grammar patterns.
Understand the main meaning of slow, clearly spoken exchanges on familiar topics.
Participate in short practical dialogues with culturally appropriate expressions.
